sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Brings in the page link tool, React helpers, the vault scene, the build, video and project data, and the asset and motion helpers.
sections.why: Gathers everything the section needs in one place.
sections.watch_out: Data file names must match real files, or the section will not build.

sections.name: AIBuilds (part 1)
sections.title: Setup and shared state
sections.what: Starts the 3D vault when WebGL is available. Tracks hover, the entered room, the wing filter, the view, the capture and the stage, and receives updates from the scene.
sections.why: Keeps the page in step with what the visitor sees in the 3D scene.
sections.watch_out: The scene is rebuilt whenever the reduced motion setting changes.

sections.name: AIBuilds (part 2)
sections.title: Escape key and room helpers
sections.what: Listens for the Escape key to step out of a room. Provides helpers to pick a wing, move between rooms (wrapping around at the ends) and count builds in each wing.
sections.why: A keyboard exit makes the 3D view easy to leave.
sections.watch_out: Room numbers wrap around, so moving past the last room leads back to the first.

sections.name: AIBuilds (part 3)
sections.title: Wing tabs and room heading
sections.what: Shows the wing tabs (all, work and fun), a hint line, and the room panel heading with the project name and punchline.
sections.why: Lets visitors filter by work or fun builds and see which room they are in.
sections.watch_out: Tab labels come from the wing data, so renaming a wing changes the buttons.

sections.name: AIBuilds (part 4)
sections.title: View switch and capture controls
sections.what: Lets the visitor switch the room panel between interface, codebase and video views. Shows a progress bar for the five lift stages, and cycles through interface captures with arrows.
sections.why: Each view shows a different part of the build, and the progress bar explains the 3D lift.
sections.watch_out: The progress bar has five stages, so changing the stage count means updating its labels too.

sections.name: AIBuilds (part 5)
sections.title: Video list and stack list
sections.what: Lists the video slots with READY or AWAITING FILE status and plays the chosen video in the media view. Also lists the technology stack by layer, the AI features and the source, with links to the deep dive page and GitHub.
sections.why: Shows the project's stack and videos without leaving the room.
sections.watch_out: A video only plays while the media view is open, and a missing file shows as awaiting.

sections.name: AIBuilds (part 6)
sections.title: Build controls and bottom bar
sections.what: Shows the Repo and Live links for the selected build, Previous and Next buttons for moving between rooms, a list of all builds to jump to, and a link to the full archive. It also shows the simple fallback list when 3D graphics are unavailable.
sections.why: Lets visitors move through the builds and reach the code, the live site, or the full archive.
sections.watch_out: The Previous and Next buttons assume a room has been entered, so any change to how that state is set can break them.

sections.name: FallbackList
sections.title: Fallback list without 3D
sections.what: A plain grid of build cards, each with its first picture, code, name and punchline, linking to that build's page. It appears in place of the 3D scene when WebGL is not available.
sections.why: Lets every visitor see the builds even when the 3D view cannot run.
sections.watch_out: A build with no screenshots shows no picture at all, because the picture is only drawn when a first shot exists.

summary: The AI builds section: a 3D vault of rooms, one per build, with filters for work and fun builds and a side panel for the room the visitor has entered.
purpose: Lets visitors walk into each AI project and see its interface capture, architecture, and videos.
why: Likely reason: each project is presented as a room for a memorable feel, while the readable details sit in a panel.
how: 1. Checks for WebGL and loads the vault scene. 2. Tracks hover, the entered room, the wing filter, the view, the capture and the stage. 3. Shows a hover card for rooms and a side panel for an entered room. 4. The panel offers view buttons, capture arrows, a stage bar, a video list and an architecture list. 5. The Escape key steps out of a room.
inputs: Vault build data, video slot data, project data, WebGL support, the reduced motion setting, the screen width, the mode (calm or technical), and the visitor's actions.
outputs: A 3D vault, a side panel with project details, links to the deep dive page and to GitHub when provided, and video players.
risks: The section depends on several data files. A missing video or capture shows as awaiting, which is a safe fallback. Mode changes the text between plain and technical wording.
debug: If the vault does not appear, check WebGL and the scene import. If a room panel is empty, check that build's entry in the data. If a video does not play, check its file name and asset path.
